### Modifications in Each File

#### File: `arch/x86/kernel/machine_kexec_32.c`
1. In `machine_kexec_free_page_tables` function:
   - After every `free_page` call for the page directory (pgd), page middle directory (pmd0, pmd1), and page table entries (pte0, pte1), the corresponding pointer is set to `NULL`. This prevents dangling pointers after the pages have been freed.

2. In `machine_kexec_alloc_page_tables` function:
   - The call to `machine_kexec_free_page_tables(image)` has been removed when memory allocation fails, allowing for proper clean-up to be handled elsewhere.

#### File: `arch/x86/kernel/machine_kexec_64.c`
1. In `free_transition_pgtable` function:
   - Similar to the changes in the 32-bit file, `NULL` assignments are added for `p4d`, `pud`, `pmd`, and `pte` after each respective `free_page` call to avoid dangling pointers.

2. In `init_transition_pgtable` function:
   - The removal of the `free_transition_pgtable(image)` call upon encountering an error allows for better management of memory and prevents double freeing.

### Relationships of Modifications
The modifications in both files address the same issue of preventing double freeing of memory pages when memory allocation fails. The changes establish a consistent error handling mechanism, ensuring that memory cleanup is centralized in the `machine_kexec_cleanup` function instead of being redundantly called in multiple locations. This reduces the risk of crashes due to double frees during the kernel's kexec loading process. The `NULL` assignments improve safety by ensuring that freed pointers do not lead to potential dereferencing issues later in the program flow.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug is caused by the `free_transition_pgtable()` function being called multiple times due to error handling in both `init_transition_pgtable()` and `machine_kexec_cleanup()`, leading to a double free of memory pages when memory allocation fails during the kexec loading process. This occurs because both functions attempt to free the same page tables without proper checks to prevent double freeing.
        
        Commit message:
        x86/kexec: Avoid double free_page() upon do_kexec_load()
 failure

>From ff82bedd3e12f0d3353282054ae48c3bd8c72012 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tetsuo Handa <penguin-kernel@I-love.SAKURA.ne.jp>
Date: Wed, 9 May 2018 12:12:39 +0900
Subject: [PATCH v3] x86/kexec: avoid double free_page() upon do_kexec_load() failure.

syzbot is reporting crashes after memory allocation failure inside
do_kexec_load() [1]. This is because free_transition_pgtable() is called
by both init_transition_pgtable() and machine_kexec_cleanup() when memory
allocation failed inside init_transition_pgtable().

Regarding 32bit code, machine_kexec_free_page_tables() is called by both
machine_kexec_alloc_page_tables() and machine_kexec_cleanup() when memory
allocation failed inside machine_kexec_alloc_page_tables().

Fix this by leaving the error handling to machine_kexec_cleanup()
(and optionally setting NULL after free_page()).

[1] https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?id=91e52396168cf2bdd572fe1e1bc0bc645c1c6b40

Fixes: f5deb79679af6eb4 ("x86: kexec: Use one page table in x86_64 machine_kexec")
Fixes: 92be3d6bdf2cb349 ("kexec/i386: allocate page table pages dynamically")
Reported-by: syzbot <syzbot+d96f60296ef613fe1d69@syzkaller.appspotmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Tetsuo Handa <penguin-kernel@I-love.SAKURA.ne.jp>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Acked-by: Baoquan He <bhe@redhat.com>
Cc: thomas.lendacky@amd.com
Cc: prudo@linux.vnet.ibm.com
Cc: Huang Ying <ying.huang@intel.com>
Cc: syzkaller-bugs@googlegroups.com
Cc: takahiro.akashi@linaro.org
Cc: H. Peter Anvin <hpa@zytor.com>
Cc: akpm@linux-foundation.org
Cc: dyoung@redhat.com
Cc: kirill.shutemov@linux.intel.com
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/201805091942.DGG12448.tMFVFSJFQOOLHO@I-love.SAKURA.ne.jp  
        
        Patch:
         
 static void machine_kexec_free_page_tables(struct kimage *image)
 {
 	free_page((unsigned long)image->arch.pgd);
+	image->arch.pgd = NULL;
 #ifdef CONFIG_X86_PAE
 	free_page((unsigned long)image->arch.pmd0);
+	image->arch.pmd0 = NULL;
 	free_page((unsigned long)image->arch.pmd1);
+	image->arch.pmd1 = NULL;
 #endif
 	free_page((unsigned long)image->arch.pte0);
+	image->arch.pte0 = NULL;
 	free_page((unsigned long)image->arch.pte1);
+	image->arch.pte1 = NULL;
 }
 
 #endif
 	    !image->arch.pte0 || !image->arch.pte1) {
-		machine_kexec_free_page_tables(image);
 		return -ENOMEM;
 	}
